security_privacy_cost_impact: Tightens only, and only against later drift: nothing reachable on the clean set changes. Within what plan section 5 states the fingerprint reads, and subject to its stated exclusions (types, operators, casts and the rest; the catalog functions the reading itself calls, which a perfect superuser forgery could replace): a later file that redefines, renames, moves, re-grants or re-owns any function (its prosrc or SQL-standard body included), relation, schema or language initdb made (OID below 16384, in any schema), or that replaces the fingerprint's own table, makes a client role superuser, bypassrls, createrole, createdb, inherit, login or replication, sets a default setting for a client role or for every role, makes an event trigger, adds a default privilege for PUBLIC, anon or authenticated, or grants a client CREATE or a grant option on any other database now fails migrate-clean by name. As first written (0f08d92) this sentence was broader than the batch read: C0 F1 (a view swapped in for the reference) and C0 F2 (a rename) passed every layer, and A1 R1 (an SQL-standard body) was unread; 129's review round closed all three (plan section 9). migrate-clean creates schema catalog_baseline and table catalog_baseline.system_fingerprint (revoked from PUBLIC) in the test database before the first migration; it holds catalog text only. No data, secret or cost impact; migrate-clean takes about 5 s.
migration_and_data_impact: NONE. Batch 129 adds no migration and needs no migration number; it changes catalog probes and the migrate-clean executor, a driver comment, static tests and the README. The test database gains catalog_baseline.system_fingerprint, written by migrate-clean only; no migration creates it.
compatibility_impact: Additive. Tests stay 677 and cases 1079; foundation-contract's assertion floor 500 -> 525 (no test added or renamed); catalog probes 23 -> 24. A later batch that must change or rename an initdb object, a client role attribute, a role default for a client or for every role, an event trigger, a default privilege for a client or a client's privilege on another database fails migrate-clean and must change the rule with its reason. A database first migrated before 129 and reset with reset-test keeps a fingerprint taken after those migrations; CI uses a fresh cluster.
known_limitations: The system object fingerprint does not read (plan §5): types, domains, operators (ALTER OPERATOR ... SET (RESTRICT = ...) on an initdb operator), casts, operator classes and families, collations, conversions, text-search objects, aggregates' pg_aggregate rows, a type ACL; pg_database, pg_authid and tablespace rows; parameter ACLs but session_replication_role's; an object a migration makes and drops again; a hostile superuser migration that perfectly rewrites the output functions or operators the readings call (the in-memory comparison of 129's review round takes the reference relation out of reach, not those functions); the platform's managed schemas. Cross-minor-version stability is stated, measured on 17.11 only. The fingerprint is not placed in every probe job; a drift aimed at blinding one probe is held by that probe's self-test. Owed, as owed: the Owner ended the hardening chain at 129.
C0 F2 (C0 N3 on 127's re-check): a looser permissive SELECT sibling on a client-readable, non-writable table is held by rls-smoke alone; the permissive policy probe reads client-writable tables only.

A client-encoding change whose name or SET words are computed at run time (concatenation, chr(), format(), convert_from(); EXECUTE of a SET built in a DO body) is outside psqlLex's list; the static spellings (U&, E'') are refused since batch 128. Owed.
A function reached through an operator is not read by the policy helper probe's called-function rule (Q0 N5, INFO); the deparse pins hold it on client-writable tables.

The other roles' reach (app_worker, service_role, RFC-2026-023 command roles) is read by no rule here, for RFC-2026-023's disposition; with it blocker 186's (15) command-role half, (16) (the anonymisation route batch 160 needs) and (20) stay owed.

A constant-true narrowing spelled without OR, TRUE or NOT (1 = 1) is not read statically; the three owner-UPDATE permissive policies (workspaces, workspace_settings, workspace_invitations) have no bare-UPDATE case of their own.
The client schema and membership probes model the CI shim; on the platform the managed schemas grant clients USAGE and authenticator is a member of the client roles, and the probes do not run there.
Remedy (b), created_by out of the client INSERT grant, is not taken, by the Owner's answer of 2026-10-03. 122's service-path closures are pinned by exact deparse in no probe.

allow_system_table_mods set by a name computed at run time passes the lexer by design; what it enables is read by OID (X2c, X2bc). The pg_catalog guard reads relations, functions, operators and casts, not other object kinds, in an initdb schema.

129's review round (plan section 9.6): the table's identity is not re-checked inside the probe job (C0 F1 remedy (b), second half; the verdict on the migrations no longer reads the table), and CLIENT_ROLE_SETTINGS and PINNED_EVENT_TRIGGERS are pinned empty as the CI shim measures, so a platform that sets a client role default or carries event triggers would be refused by name until pinned with its reason.
